assertions_contracts.best_practice: Unchanged through 0.16 and not altered by the 0.17 release notes as far as this pass could verify: asserts are for established invariants, comptime for provable properties, and unreachable remains a correctness claim whose violation is illegal behaviour in unsafe modes. The guide's insistence on testing rejection in ReleaseFast matches upstream's own warning that safety checks are mode-dependent.
assertions_contracts.evidence: The guide's citations [Z1]/[Z2] are the 0.16.0 language reference and release notes, internally correct for its pin. 0.17.0 (2026-10-01) is now the current release - see toolchain_pins; no 0.17 change to assert/unreachable semantics was found in this pass, so the prescription holds and the stale surface is the pin, recorded once under toolchain_pins
assertions_contracts.guide_position: std.debug.assert for internal invariants (one per assert), comptime checks for static properties, unreachable never as a fallback or for external failure.

bounded_work.best_practice: No upstream equivalent policy exists - bounding is an application discipline in Zig, and the unmanaged-container, capacity-explicit container design the guide reflects remains the upstream direction.
bounded_work.evidence: The guide's container section matches the 0.16 unmanaged migration; nothing in the 0.17 release coverage fetched in this pass revises container capacity discipline. Pin currency is under toolchain_pins
bounded_work.guide_position: Named *_max constants for loops, allocations, retries, queues, nesting and captured output; explicit stacks instead of unbounded recursion; retries idempotent with a shared deadline.

concurrency.best_practice: The interface-based Io model the guide describes (I/O as a parameter, Threaded/Evented backends, futures/groups, cancellation as an error path) remains upstream's direction; language-level async from pre-0.15 examples is gone.
concurrency.evidence: The 0.16.0 release notes are the guide's own cited source for the Io migration. The guide was not re-verified line-by-line against 0.17's Io surface in this pass - that check belongs to the re-pin proposal under toolchain_pins; no fetched 0.17 source contradicts the model itself
concurrency.guide_position: Pass the Io dependency explicitly (0.16 interface-based I/O), bound group size, cancel and await owned work before freeing its data, cancellation is a real error path, thread-safe allocator does not imply thread-safe objects.

error_handling.best_practice: Error unions remain Zig's sole error mechanism and the documented idiom is unchanged: specific error sets, try to propagate, catch for a stated recovery, defer/errdefer for cleanup. Neither 0.16 nor 0.17 added exceptions or a generic anyerror recommendation.
error_handling.evidence: Guide text is unchanged since run 1 held this aspect and still names no C-interop route (grep-verified in this pass: no translate-c / @cImport / addTranslateC anywhere in SKILL.md or the full guide). The @cImport deprecation that run 1's proposal rests on is reconfirmed in 0.17 release coverage (deprecated, not removed). One 0.17 language change to re-check at re-pin: errdefer can no longer capture values - the guide's section 7 does not use captured errdefer, so no contradiction
error_handling.guide_position: Documented error unions on fallible paths, no anyerror on public surfaces, try propagates, catch only for a specific recovery, defer/errdefer never double-free, no catch unreachable on external failure, OOM or config.

formatting.best_practice: zig fmt is the official formatter shipped with the compiler and remains the single sanctioned style; upstream style is likewise the 4-space layout the formatter produces, not hand style.
formatting.evidence: The guide's formatter claim matches both its pin and the current release; 0.17's zig fmt additionally renames deprecated builtins in formatted code (@intFromEnum/@enumFromInt -> @backingInt/@fromBackingInt), which the guide's examples do not use
formatting.guide_position: zig fmt owns formatting (~100-col readable lines, ~70-line functions as review aids), zig fmt --check in CI, never fight its output.

memory_ownership.best_practice: The allocator-explicit discipline the guide mandates (unmanaged containers by default, allocator passed per operation, caller-buffer/fixed-capacity first) remains idiomatic upstream style; DebugAllocator is the renamed general-purpose allocator in this line.
memory_ownership.evidence: Guide text unchanged since run 1 held this aspect and already reflects the unmanaged migration. 0.17 std renames fetched in this pass (e.g. Allocator.dupeZ -> dupeSentinel in migration records) touch APIs the guide does not use; a full std-name sweep belongs to the re-pin pass
memory_ownership.guide_position: Allocators are parameters, never globals; caller buffers/fixed capacity preferred; defer/errdefer discipline with a documented freeing allocator; never mix allocators; arena is not a bound; std.testing.allocator in tests.

security.best_practice: Upstream's position is the same: ReleaseSafe for deployed code, explicit checks that survive ReleaseFast, and suspicion of FFI/process/build-script boundaries; the Zig project moved development off GitHub to Codeberg in late 2025, which affects where pinned source is fetched from.
security.evidence: Guide text unchanged since run 1 held this aspect; nothing in the 0.17 material fetched in this pass contradicts it. The Codeberg migration note from run 1 stands
security.guide_position: FFI/casts/int-to-pointer/dynamic loading/build scripts/child processes are privileged boundaries; argv-form child processes; ReleaseSafe preferred for safety-sensitive production; reviewed crypto only.

static_analysis.best_practice: Zig still ships no official linter or static analyzer comparable to clang-tidy: the compiler's own diagnostics, safety checks and ZLS diagnostics are the whole official story. The gap is the ecosystem's, not a guide error - but the guide never says this, leaving a reader to wonder which tool fills the slot its sibling guides fill with clang-tidy.
static_analysis.evidence: Unchanged from run 1 and re-verified by full read in this pass: neither SKILL.md nor the full guide names an analyzer or states that none exists upstream. (The stale ZLS situation under 0.17 is recorded under toolchain_pins, not here.)
static_analysis.guide_position: No analyzer is named: the SKILL pairing is zls + zig fmt + lldb-dap, and assurance rests on compiler diagnostics, runtime safety checks and testing across build modes.

testing.best_practice: zig test with std.testing remains the official route, and the toolchain's built-in fuzzing support (present in 0.16, carried into 0.17) remains the standard supplement for parser-shaped code, which the guide does not mention - an addition, not a correction.
testing.evidence: Guide text unchanged since run 1 (grep-verified in this pass: no fuzzing mention anywhere in the skill). The fuzzing gap is carried forward as a proposal below. Independent 0.17 migration records confirm trees build, test and fuzz under 0.17, so the proposal survives the re-pin
testing.guide_position: std.testing boundary cases, std.testing.allocator for owned allocations, allocation-failure injection per acquisition step, tests run in Debug, ReleaseSafe and ReleaseFast so rejection survives disabled safety checks.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Zig 0.17.0, released 2026-10-01 (announcement 2026-10-02), is the current stable release; master is 0.18.0-dev. 0.17 is a breaking release (split build system, removed array-multiplication syntax, renamed builtins, deprecated @cImport) and its release notes state the build-system split currently breaks ZLS integration, with the Build Server Protocol as the intended restore path - so a re-pin is a migration, and no version-matched stable ZLS for 0.17 was verified in this pass
toolchain_pins.evidence: Run 1 (same date) recorded 0.16.0 as current with master at 0.17.0-dev; that is superseded. This pass: the official download index and 0.17.0 release-notes/announcement URLs exist and are referenced by the release's own ecosystem; multiple independent migration records (projects re-pinning on 2026-10-02/04) and the Ziggit forum confirm 0.17.0 shipped 2026-10-01, its binaries are on the official download page, and master now reports 0.18.0-dev. NOTE: this audit's direct fetch of ziglang.org was unreliable (the index fetch returned a stale snapshot and the release-notes fetch returned HTTP 403, as in run 1), so the release fact rests on the official URLs plus convergent secondary records - flagged in the final report. Concrete guide impact: the section 31 reference module uses the removed array-multiplication syntax ('[_]i64{0} ** item_count_max' and the item_count_max + 1 variant), so the guide's own reference code does not compile under 0.17; the build/optimize naming and @typeInfo/std.meta surfaces also changed, per 0.17 migration records - all to be swept in the re-pin proposal below, NOT as a mechanical pin swap
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Pin Zig 0.16.0 exactly (compiler, target triple, libc, optimisation mode); copy signatures only from that version's stdlib; sources [Z1]/[Z2] cite the 0.16.0 language reference and release notes; zls for LSP (unversioned in the guide), zig fmt, lldb-dap.

current_versions.ZLS: No version-matched stable ZLS for Zig 0.17 verified in this pass: 0.17 release notes state the maker/configurer split breaks ZLS integration and the Build Server Protocol is in progress to restore it; ZLS 0.16.0 (May 2026) matches the guide's pin
current_versions.Zig: 0.17.0, released 2026-10-01 (announcement 2026-10-02) - current stable; master is 0.18.0-dev; guide pins 0.16.0 (2026-04-13); project development hosted on Codeberg
current_versions.lldb-dap: Generic LLVM DAP adapter; Zig 0.17 upgrades its bundled LLVM to the 22.1.x line (22.1.8 in release coverage); Zig has no language-specific debugger - pairing is a diver-config choice
current_versions.zig fmt: Built into the toolchain (0.16.0 as pinned; 0.17.0 current); canonical formatter; 0.17 fmt also renames deprecated builtins it formats

proposals.evidence: 0.17.0 shipped 2026-10-01 with breaking changes that reach into the guide's own text: array multiplication removed (the section 31 reference module's '**' expressions), @intFromEnum/@enumFromInt renamed to @backingInt/@fromBackingInt, errdefer can no longer capture values, @Type replaced by dedicated builtins in the 0.16/0.17 line, build-system split (configurer/maker) with changed optimize naming, and ZLS integration broken pending the Build Server Protocol. A pin-string swap would leave the guide internally false, which is why mechanical_fixes is empty for this language
proposals.proposal: Re-baseline the guide to Zig 0.17.0 as a migration pass, not a pin swap: re-run the section 31 reference module under 0.17 (replace '**' with @splat), sweep sections 2/19/20/26/27 for build, process, Io and std renames, re-point sources [Z1]/[Z2] at the 0.17.0 documentation set, and record the ZLS state honestly (0.17-matched ZLS not yet stable; editor diagnostics degraded until the Build Server Protocol lands)
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as the next Zig guide pass; until it lands, the guide must be read as a 0.16.0 guide - its internal discipline holds at that pin

proposals.evidence: Carried forward from run 1 (not applied; pass-2 addendum leaves all per-language proposals open): the toolchain's test/build system includes fuzzing of test inputs in both 0.16 and 0.17; the guide's testing section relies solely on enumerated boundary cases, the exact weakness fuzzing addresses for parsers
proposals.proposal: Add Zig's built-in fuzzing (zig build test --fuzz / fuzzable test cases) to the testing workflow for byte parsers and decoders, alongside the existing Debug/ReleaseSafe/ReleaseFast matrix.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt for parser-shaped code; keep the enumerated boundary matrix as the deterministic gate and treat fuzzing as a corpus-growing supplement.

proposals.evidence: Carried forward from run 1 (not applied) and strengthened: @cImport deprecation in favour of translate-c (b.addTranslateC()) is listed in both the 0.16 and 0.17 breaking/deprecating changes; the guide's language-specific section lists five review boundaries (allocator, borrow, build-mode safety, comptime cost, C ABI) without naming how C headers should now be consumed (grep-verified absent in this pass)
proposals.proposal: Name the current C-interop route in the FFI/security sections: prefer translate-c via the build system over @cImport, which 0.16 deprecates and 0.17 continues to deprecate - otherwise readers will copy pre-0.16 @cImport snippets the guide elsewhere warns against transplanting.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a one-paragraph addition to sections 18/26, folded into the 0.17 re-baseline pass above
